Here’s a quick, no‑frills “pre‑Product‑Hunt launch checklist” that will make sure your Lovable app (built on Supabase + Stripe) looks polished, performs smoothly, and gets the attention it deserves. Click each item when you’ve finished it so you can cross‑off with confidence. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | How to Tackle It | |---|------------|----------------|------------------| | **1** | **Finalize the app’s core experience** | Product Hunt users want to see a *working demo*, not a cliff‑hanger. | Run a full‑thru test: login, key flows, Stripe checkout, Supabase data persistence. Make sure nothing crashes. | | **2** | **Polish the UI & UX** | First impressions drive clicks. | Clean up typo‑free text, consistent spacing, brand colors. Add subtle animations for hover/click. | | **3** | **Create high‑quality screenshots & GIFs** | Visuals are what people skim first. | Capture the main screens (dashboard, checkout, profile). Show the “Lovable” feature in action. Use app‑capturing tools (Camtasia, Loom, or built‑in browser dev tools). | | **4** | **Write a Hook‑ing One‑Liner & Description** | Heading Tells the story; description turns curiosity into clicks. | 1‑2 sentence hook (e‑punch line). 3‑4 sentence description that focuses on pain‑point solved *and* the core benefit. | | **5** | **Prepare a short demo video** | Even a 30‑second clip sells features faster than a page. | Keep it under 90 seconds: intro‑brief, go‑through, call‑to‑action. Upload to YouTube and embed on Product Hunt. | | **6** | **Test strategy‑and‑billing logic** | Stripe integration errors can kill a launch. | Confirm test‑mode works end‑to‑end (checkout, invoicing, webhooks). Verify Supabase tables receive data, use real payment flow in test mode. | | **7** | **Set up a dedicated product‑hunt email address** | Helps you filter the incoming messages. | Create something like `producthunt@lovable.app` or use a forwarder. | | **8** | **Add a real‑time analytics dashboard** | Quantify traffic and usage within minutes. | Integrate Plausible, Mixpanel or PostHog (free tiers). | | **9** | **Write a privacy policy & Terms of Service** | Needed for Stripe, Supabase & for trust. | Use tools like Termly or the free templates from Open Source license; have a legal‑friendly version covering user data, cookies, refunds, etc. | | **10** | **Price & free trial / demo config** | People need a clear entry point. | Decide: free tier (limited usage), free demo, or 14‑day trial. Turbo‑run the Stripe plans and test the flows. | | **11** | **Set up a landing page ready to receive traffic** | You’ll drop users onto the product‑hunt link. | Simple hub with the app name, tagline, screenshots, demo link (maybe use ShareGPT or you’re at small preview). | | **12** | **Create a press kit** | Makes it easy for community members and journalists. | Include logo (SVG + PNG), screenshots, app description, founder bios, a few key quotes, a short video embed link. Store it in a public S3 bucket or private Google Drive with read‑only. | | **13** | **Build an “early‑adopter” mailing list** | Capture interest for future marketing. | Use a simple Sign-Up form on the landing page (Mailchimp, ConvertKit or Supabase auth + email). Offer a small incentive (e.g. “Get 2 weeks of premium for free”). | | **14** | **Plan the “launch day” timeline** | Helps you stay coordinated and ready. | | • 09:00 PM PST – Soft‑launch
• 10:00 PM PST – Go live on Product‑Hunt
• 11:00 PM PST – Tweet/ FB post
• 12:00 AM PST – Discord announcement (if you have a community)
• 02:00 AM PST – Review feedback | | **15** | **Prepare a FAQ** | Saves you time answering repetitive questions. | Cover pricing, Stripe refunds, Supabase data privacy, and “what next?”. | | **16** | **Test on multiple browsers/devices** | Catch layout issues early. | Chrome, Safari, Firefox, mobile—ensure responsive. | | **17** | **Enable rate‑limiting & error monitoring** | Protect your infrastructure during launch spikes. | Use Supabase’s built‑in monitoring, Sentry or PostHog error logs. | | **18** | **Make a Discord / Slack channel for supporters** | Vital community building. | Create a public channel on Discord or Slack. Invite early testers and label it “Launch”. | | **19** | **Confirm your domain’s SSL & email deliverability** | Cold emails or newsletters won’t hit inbox otherwise. | Use a verified CNAME for SPF/MX, check DMARC, keep an SPF/DKIM set. | | **20** | **Write a short, enthusiastic launch tweet** | Product Hunt posts often get 90% of their traffic from Twitter. | “🚀 New launch: – Build faster & cheaper with Supabase & Stripe 🚀 #ProductHunt @producthunt” | --- ### Final Double‑Check (quick‑scan) - [ ] All links work (App, Landing, Demo, Purchase) - [ ] Screenshots/imagery are high‑resolution and reflect the latest build - [ ] Stripe has fresh test keys and live keys toggled correctly - [ ] Supabase is set to production mode (don’t forget to switch environment) - [ ] Privacy policy & ToS are linked from landing & app - [ ] You have at least one demo user ready to walk through the app - [ ] Product Hunt account is ready, and you’ve filled in the description fields - [ ] You’ve left a “hot‑key” button or snippet on your landing page so visitors can sign up instantly --- ### One Final Thought Product Hunt nights are about **human interaction**—people want to talk, ask questions, and feel part of a community.
